turns.t: Right, I'm here for my regular check. Lithium levels and all that.
Good to see you. How have you been since the last visit?
Steady, mostly. A bit of a tremor in my hands again, mind.
Is it constant, or does it come and go?
Worse when I hold a cup. Settles when I rest my hands.
Any other changes, thirst, passing more urine, or tummy upset?
No thirst. No tummy upset.
And your mood? ~
Level. No highs and no lows for a good few months now. ~
Doctor, I took his blood this morning for the lithium level. The lab says it'll be ready by this afternoon. ~
Thank you. Are you drinking enough water in this heat? ~
Plenty. A couple of litres. ~
Good, because dehydration can raise the lithium level. And are you taking any painkillers, like ibuprofen? ~
No, I was told to avoid them. Only paracetamol. ~
That's right. Any allergies I should record?
When I was a child, I came out in a rash with penicillin. They told me to avoid it, and I have.
Thank you. Any operations in your history?
Just my appendix, when I was nineteen.
And are you drinking or smoking?
No smoking. I have a pint now and then.
Good. I'd like to explain what we do with the level today. ~
Go on. ~
If it's within the usual range, we carry on exactly as we are. If it's high, I'll phone you the same day.
Fine. I'll keep my phone on. ~
Please don't change your dose yourself, and keep up the water.
I won't. ~
I'd also like to see you in three months for the routine check, and we'll look at your kidneys and thyroid again.
Three months. All right. ~
I'll book that for you before you leave. ~
Thank you both. ~
